title: Correlated Gaussian integral for integrable products
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be such that $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is integrable under the joint distribution of $(X,Y)$ formed from independent $X,W\sim\gamma_n$ by setting $Y=\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,W$. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(y)\,d\mathcal L(X,Y)(x,y)=\int f(x)\left(\int g\bigl(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,w\bigr)\,d\gamma_n(w)\right)d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure and $\mathcal L(X,Y)$ denotes that joint measure.
hypotheses_covered: $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is integrable with respect to the correlated Gaussian measure
